html:
Saint-John Perse was the pen name of Alexis Leger, a poet and diplomat born in Pointe-a-Pitre, Guadeloupe, in 1887, who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1960.

His family, white Creole planters, left the island for France when he was a boy. His early poems recall a childhood among the islands. As a senior official of the French foreign ministry he helped shape policy in the 1930s, and he went into exile in America when France fell in 1940.

His long poem Anabasis was translated by T. S. Eliot. He is the first Nobel laureate from the French Caribbean, before Maryse Conde won fame from the same island and Derek Walcott from St Lucia.
